Since $d_i > 1$, the product of any two distinct generators $x_i x_j$ ($i \neq j$) is non-zero and has degree $d_i + d_j$. The product of a generator with itself is zero.
So, as a vector space over $\mathbb{Q}$, $R$ has a basis consisting of all possible products of distinct generators:
- Degree 0: $1$
- Degree $d_i$: $x_i$ (3 elements)
- Degree $d_i + d_j$ ($i<j$): $x_i x_j$ (3 elements)
- Degree $d_1+d_2+d_3$: $x_1 x_2 x_3$ (1 element)
Total dimension = $1 + 3 + 3 + 1 = 8$.
